::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 20th [<i>c</i>. 1880]  
**From:** “Monthly Packet” 6, Paternoster Row, London, E.C.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear [Miss Routledge](people/person_1264.qmd)

King Charles will come - if the [Cameos](cmy_books/cmybook_213.qmd) and their author and the [Monthly packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) survive so long - in his due season - which cannot well be anticipated.[^1] But I am afraid a defence out of the Monthly Packet would not satisfy his enemies. Would it not be better to go to the fountain head? Clarendon’s [History of the Rebellion](other_books/otherbook_35.qmd) is not a book hard to get at. 

Or Guizot’s [history of the English Rebellion](other_books/otherbook_1100.qmd) which is a very <u>fair</u> book, and being the judgment of a statesman cannot be sneered at.

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The 'Cameos from English History' series in *MP* reached the reign of Charles I in March 1884.
